SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. Do not transmit an unknown proper name by spelling. Refer to the named entity by its role, properties, or relations, then give it a discourse alias.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. Do not transmit an unknown proper name by spelling. Refer to the named entity by its role, properties, or relations, then give it a discourse alias.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. Do not transmit an unknown proper name by spelling. Refer to the named entity by its role, properties, or relations, then give it a discourse alias.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY

𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.

𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.

PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.

Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.

𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.

A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. 𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. Do not transmit an unknown proper name by spelling. Refer to the named entity by its role, properties, or relations, then give it a discourse alias.

𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. Do not transmit an unknown proper name by spelling. Refer to the named entity by its role, properties, or relations, then give it a discourse alias.

𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.

𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.

𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. Do not transmit an unknown proper name by spelling. Refer to the named entity by its role, properties, or relations, then give it a discourse alias.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. Do not transmit an unknown proper name by spelling. Refer to the named entity by its role, properties, or relations, then give it a discourse alias.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. Do not transmit an unknown proper name by spelling. Refer to the named entity by its role, properties, or relations, then give it a discourse alias.

SWARMISH — semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
All public messages must contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information that is already mutually recoverable.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
The predicate determines the natural semantic interpretation of its roles: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; EQUAL uses actor and theme as compared items. For a property predicate, actor is the thing having the property. For KNOW/SAY/REQUEST the theme can be a nested proposition. A recipient can identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a semantic description: first is head, following words restrict it. For example vessel water describes a water-associated vessel, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. Compounds are semantic descriptions, not encodings of English spellings. Familiar discourse entities may be referred to by a short distinguishing description.
A markerless content phrase is permitted only as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear from the preceding exchange. A bare predicate may be used when all its roles are mutually understood. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
The following scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They can also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause when scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put an unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it already is true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause as uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow it by two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one of which holds.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
AGENTS AND REFERENCE
Literal agent IDs are complete entity names and can fill any role. First-person, second-person, unknown-value, reference, and discourse aliases will be listed below. Do not transmit an unknown proper name by spelling. Refer to the named entity by its role, properties, or relations, then give it a discourse alias.

SWARMISH — complete semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
Public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information already mutually recoverable. Freely choose synonyms; never choose by a turn schedule, sender identity, counting, or calculation.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
Predicate determines interpretation: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; OWNED-BY uses actor=possession/theme=owner; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; CAUSES uses actor=cause/theme=effect. Other binary relations normally use actor=described thing/theme=reference thing. GIVE uses actor=sender/theme=item/recipient=receiver. Property predicates use actor=thing having property. KNOW/SAY/BELIEVE take a nested proposition as theme. KNOW claims established information; BELIEVE does not. WANT is preference; REQUEST is a speech act. Use recipient to identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a description: first is head, following words restrict it. A container liquid is a liquid-associated container, not two clauses. Use nested clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous. A nested clause following a head describes that head; its omitted actor refers to the head. Thus a person followed by a repair-action clause describes a repairer. A nested clause alone as a role value denotes the proposition/event, not a person.
𘅌𘉝 groups a pair of phrases: follow it with two complete clauses or two individual content words/aliases. It denotes the pair as one value. For complex entity descriptions first bind aliases, then group those aliases. Do not use mere adjacency to mean two independent entities.
A markerless content phrase is permitted as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear. A bare predicate is permitted when its roles are mutually understood. A single unnested clause may omit its outer opening/closing words when the roles remain clear; scoped or embedded clauses must retain boundaries. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
Scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. They may also govern a single content word or alias, but use a clause if scope could be unclear.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put the unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert it is already true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow with two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one holding.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
The conjunction and alternative operators may also join two individual content words/aliases as a grouped semantic phrase; for complex descriptions use clauses or aliases. Scope is always the explicitly following unit(s), not the rest of the message.
AGENTS, REFERENCE, AND OPEN VOCABULARY
Literal agent IDs are complete names. Self means current sender; addressee means intended recipient and must be made explicit if unclear. Unknown names cannot be spelled: identify their task-visible role, properties, location, or relationships. Quoted propositions are semantic reports, not exact arbitrary external strings. There is no literal spelling escape.

Questions: use unknown-value as actor for WHO, theme for WHAT/WHICH, quantity parameter for HOW-MANY, source for WHY, or setting for WHEN/WHERE. Include category/place/time words to disambiguate. A question without unknown-value is yes/no. True/correct and false/incorrect serve as yes/no replies.
𗿃𘏛 identify/bind alias to a particular referent; 𗿃𘖾 define alias as category/property/action; 𗿃𗜎 define alias as proposition. These are predicates: theme is the alias and attribute is its description or a complete clause. Binding persists in shared discourse until an explicit new binding of the same alias.
